Getting stuck in a loop of repetitive thoughts, often called rumination, can be incredibly exhausting. When you find yourself caught in this cycle, it helps to gently break your focus by engaging your senses in the present moment. Try a grounding exercise, like splashing cold water on your face or naming five things you can see around you. Shifting your attention to a physical activity, like going for a brisk walk, can also give your brain a much-needed break. 

Another helpful strategy is to write the thought down. Putting it on paper can signal to your brain that the concern is safely recorded and no longer needs to be constantly reviewed. If these repetitive thoughts are causing significant distress or interfering with your daily life, consider reaching out to a mental health professional. They can help you explore the root of these thoughts and teach you personalized techniques to manage them.
